Summary of triage (first 20 minutes):
- Observed: US-dedicated GPU pool for Argentum is saturated. GPU utilization at 100% across several nodes; queue depth elevated; KV cache miss rate jumped ~4x.
- Symptoms: increased token generation latency, request timeouts and downstream 5xx responses due to queueing and occasional OOM-triggered restarts on a small subset of pods.
- Likely cause: sudden traffic spike with higher average seq lengths; combined with a model variant that is memory-heavy (float16 unfused kernels). No infra deployment in last 48 hours.

Short-term mitigations (recommended now):
1) Apply per-account soft-throttle at the routing layer (reduce concurrency per-session to 60%) — can be applied in 2–5 minutes.
2) Route a fraction (~30%) of Argentum traffic to a lower-memory, slightly faster model variant (quantized q4_* fallback) to relieve memory pressure — needs config change and model warmup (~6–8 minutes).
3) Temporarily raise burst cap for Argentum while we stabilize (requires exec approval for credits) — will buy ~20–30 minutes of headroom.
4) If necessary, spin a small ephemeral pool (3 GPUs) in us-east to offload hot traffic — provisioning ETA ~12–18 minutes.

Diagnostics links:
- Logs snapshot (Stackdriver): https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/argentum-diagnostics-20270329
- Infra ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-7123 (creating now)

I'll start 1) immediately and prepare 2) and 4) in parallel. Marcus — please escalate for authorization on burst credits; Monica, please coordinate customer comms and ask them to opt in for an interim model if they will.

—Rishi
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
